A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L. Content can be reliably matched across the additions, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original numerical gradient-flow experiments, including loss trajectories and gradient-ascent divergence rates in Figures 3–5 and additional experiments in Appendix L.

after.justification: V2 retains original numerical experiments and adds the general symmetric free-evolution validation in Figure 4, alongside revised gradient-ascent results in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The CP tensor models, quadratic loss, Gaussian initialization, gradient flow, and diagram/Pareto/generating-function framework remain unchanged. Appendix G.3 applies that framework to another analytically solved case rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic zero-target and identity-target tensor problems, with the same tensor orders and symmetry settings. The added free SYM ν=4 experiment varies model parameterization within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates external competing algorithms. Comparisons remain between the authors' analytical predictions and numerical gradient-flow trajectories; no baseline method is added or removed.

E3.justification: New Figure 4 uses p=64, H in {4p², p², p²/4}, E[L(0)]=1, and T=96p³σ⁶. The gradient-ascent phase map changes from p=16 in v1 Figure 5 to p=64 in v2 Figure 6, whose example trajectories specify p=256. The Euler integration and full-loss batching procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a parameter-sensitivity check across three H/p² ratios, testing the general free-evolution solution beyond the previously illustrated extreme regimes. The existing noise-boundary analysis is also revised using a larger p; the earlier appendix size-sensitivity experiments remain.

E5.justification: Both gradient-ascent divergence-rate captions report 10 independent experiments. V2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds three experimental/theoretical loss trajectories in Figure 4 and replaces the gradient-ascent heatmap and example trajectories in v1 Figure 5 with v2 Figure 6. The qualitative agreement and two-regime finding remain. These are additional or replaced results under changed settings, not same-setting performance gains; the retained appendix plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Section 7 defers general symmetric free evolutions; v2 adds Appendix G.3 with Proposition G.1, its proof, a generating-function equation, and the explicit solution for the full A–B segment for even ν≥4, including why the recurrence fails at ν=2. This substantially extends the supplied derivations. V2 also corrects mathematical slips, such as odd s_D becoming odd s_R in Appendix D.2.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, enumerated contributions, and Discussion retain the same central claims about diagram expansions, learning regimes, NTK behavior, and explicit loss solutions. The additional derivation supplies a previously deferred result without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G.3 add an explicit explanation of why general free evolution requires different treatment at ν=2 versus even ν≥4, connecting the recurrence's applicability to the contraction structure. The broader limitations concerning formal-series summation and rigorous convergence in Section 11 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix L newly supplies a repository link for the Jupyter notebooks used to reproduce the experiments. Figure 4 also documents the added experiment's parameter choices and normalization. The existing Euler discretization and memory-efficient loss-computation details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Changes such as Dyer and Gur-Ari 2019 becoming 2020 and Domine et al. 2024 becoming 2025 update publication metadata rather than introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: V2 makes widespread small copyedits, expands and locally reorders Appendix B's explanations, and adds a proof overview in Appendix D. It also adds conference publication text, a conflict-of-interest disclosure, and an impact statement. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 4 and explanatory diagrams in Appendices B and G.3, redraws Figure 1(l), corrects Figure 1(i)'s caption, and revises the gradient-ascent plot and caption. Most existing figures and both tables retain their content, with renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new general free-evolution derivation and Figure 4 replace an explicit deferral in v1, while clearer diagram explanations and the notebook link improve usability. These are focused gains, with the general convergence limitations retained. New Eq. (36) introduces a localized coefficient error: the stated Gaussian/Wick setup gives (p³+6p²+8p)Hσ⁶, rather than (p³+5p²+9p)Hσ⁶. This defect modestly offsets, but does not outweigh, the improvements.
